subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek prefix-cache protection: opaque provider-time placeholders, semantic/opt-in compaction, or heartbeat isolation/pruning?
rationale: The code can mechanically summarize payloads, but deciding which tool outputs the model may stop seeing is a product/runtime policy choice with agent-correctness and provider-cache tradeoffs.

options.title: Keep semantic results visible
options.body: Reject opaque placeholders for normal tools and require a narrow policy such as heartbeat-only handling, semantic compaction, or isolated heartbeat sessions.

options.title: Accept opaque placeholders
options.body: Maintainers can choose to prioritize cache stability and knowingly accept that selected tool calls no longer expose their results to the model.

options.title: Pause for the canonical cache policy
options.body: Hold or replace this PR after choosing how it should relate to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95311 and the linked tool-result issue.

recommendation.title: Keep semantic results visible
recommendation.body: Reject opaque placeholders for normal tools and require a narrow policy such as heartbeat-only handling, semantic compaction, or isolated heartbeat sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current history across provider replay and prompt-cache boundary behavior.
